title: Image cache regression caused hosted GPU pool depletion — RCA & mitigation plan
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
A regression in the image-cache operator introduced in the deployment of operator v2.3.1 changed eviction semantics and effectively pinned multiple large model images on a subset of hosted GPU nodes. Over ~36 hours this caused steady growth of GPU memory and local disk reserved for pinned images, preventing model instantiation for new requests. The autoscaler did not trigger fast enough due to configured hysteresis and lack of an admission fast-fail path, so the hosted API queue grew, tenants saw increased latency and throttling, and several large customers experienced request failures during the incident window.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-03-01 03:20 UTC: deployment of operator v2.3.1 (image cache changes) rolled to eu-west-1.
- 2026-03-01 08:00 UTC: first elevated GPU reserved memory alerts on node group gpool-eu-1; initial pager suppressed as metric was noisy.
- 2026-03-01 18:15 UTC: hosted-api 95th p99 latency rose above SLO, queue length increasing; on-call escalated.
- 2026-03-01 19:10 UTC: manual investigation found image count per node exceeded expected budget; image cache metrics showed 'pinned_count' stuck.
- 2026-03-01 21:00 UTC: temporary mitigations applied (forced GC, operator restart, scale reserve) — short-term relief but didn't address root cause fully.

Root cause (summary):
The operator change swapped eviction logic from an LRU/timestamp-based policy to a hybrid policy that prioritized "pinning" images referenced by the node-local prefetcher. Under a common workload pattern (many tenants concurrently prefetching different model variants), some nodes accumulated >6 large images pinned and the operator refused to evict them because pin counters were never decremented on failed model initializations. A race between model pull failure paths and the new pin accounting created permanent pin leaks until the operator was restarted. This produced sustained GPU memory reservation and prevented new model allocations, resulting in queue buildup and autoscaler starvation.

Contributing factors:
- Change was insufficiently covered by unit/integration tests for concurrent prefetch+failed-pull scenarios.
- Telemetry exposed total image count and disk reclaim, but we lacked a high-confidence alert that correlates "pinned image count" with available GPU memory headroom.
- Autoscaler hysteresis and conservative scale policy made reactive scale slow; no admission-layer fast-fail existed to shed requests when model instantiation is impossible.

Immediate mitigations executed (what we did during the incident):
1) Ran the emergency eviction script to forcibly unpin and delete stale images on affected nodes (scripts/ops/force-image-gc.sh).
2) Rolled back operator to v2.2.8 in eu-west-1 and staged rollout to other regions. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5243
3) Temporarily increased reserved capacity for hosted GPU pools to reduce immediate customer impact (scale up + pre-warm).
4) Enabled a temporary admission check to fast-fail requests that cannot be satisfied due to pinned-image exhaustion (hotfix: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8124).

Planned permanent fixes (this ticket scope):
- Fix the pin accounting bug so pin counters decrement reliably on all model-pull failure paths (owner: @ethan-z). Target: code PR and unit tests.
- Restore LRU reclaim semantics with an explicit per-node image budget and a strict eviction-on-exceed behavior. Add an override to opt-in to the hybrid behavior after validation. (owner: @maria-gleason)
- Add an integration test that simulates concurrent prefetches and failed pulls, including CI gate to prevent regressions. (owner: @devops-team)
- Implement an autoscaler signal derived from available GPU memory headroom + pinned-image count; enable reactive preemptive scale quicker and add a cooldown tuned for image-GC events. (owner: @infra-autoscale)
- Implement an admission-layer fast-decline policy that fails early when node-level resource budgets are already exhausted to prevent queue amplification. (owner: @ethan-z)
- Add persistent telemetry + alert: correlated metric (average pinned_images_per_node, gpu_memory_headroom) and an alerting rule for >80% pinned_images saturation sustained for 15m.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field) and rollout plan:
- Patch is merged and passes CI/integration tests.
- Canary rollout to 5% of capacity for operator v2.3.2 (with fixes) with enhanced telemetry for 48h.
- No new pin leaks observed in canary cluster; queue length and latency return to pre-incident baseline under the defined SLO for 72h.
- New alerts fire in the staging cluster for synthetic pin/leak inject tests.

Longer-term program items (out-of-scope for this ticket but created as follow-ups):
- Node-level image budget admission controller (ENG-420450).
- Chaos tests that intentionally leak pins to validate autoscaler + admission controller responses (ENG-420451).

Why this is different from past GPU exhaustion incidents:
Previous incidents focused on request admission, batch packing, and KV-cache pollution. This one was a runtime-image lifecycle regression that allowed per-node image accumulation to manifest as a capacity exhaustion vector. Fixes require both runtime/operator correctness and new autoscaler/admission signals.

Risks and trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive eviction can cause increased model pull churn and transient latency spikes; we will mitigate with staged canaries and a short-lived scale-up during rollout.
- Conservative autoscaler tuning avoids flapping but increases exposure time; we will tune cooldowns and use pinned-image metrics so autoscaler is targeted.

Owners and next steps (immediate):
- Ethan Zhao (@ethan-z) — implement pin counter fix, admission fast-decline, open PR by 2026-03-08.
- Maria Gleason (@maria-gleason) — operator rollback validation and LRU restore design doc due 2026-03-06.
- DevOps (/infra-autoscale) — autoscaler signal design and prototype by 2026-03-15.
- On-call/ops — scheduled node drain and capacity reserve runbooks updated.
